rn.smoke.title: There's smoke today
rn.smoke.1: Go inside and close all windows and doors.
rn.smoke.2: Set your heat or AC to recirculate so it stops pulling outside air in. If you have a window unit, close its fresh-air vent.
rn.smoke.3: Pick one room with the fewest windows. Put your air cleaner there and keep the door shut.
rn.smoke.4: Do not vacuum, burn candles, fry food, or smoke indoors. All of it adds particles to air you are trying to clean.
rn.smoke.5: Skip outdoor exercise. Skip indoor exercise too if you can smell smoke inside.
rn.smoke.6: Asthma, COPD, or a heart condition? Keep your inhaler or medication within reach and follow your action plan.
rn.smoke.7: Wear an N95 or KN95 if you must go out. Cloth and surgical masks do not filter smoke.
rn.smoke.8: If your home cannot get clean, go to a clean air location.
rn.smoke.911: Trouble breathing, chest pain, or confusion is an emergency. Call 911.
rn.quake.title: There was just an earthquake
rn.quake.1: Check yourself, then the people near you. For serious bleeding, press hard on the wound and keep pressing.
rn.quake.2: Put shoes on before you walk anywhere. Broken glass causes most injuries after a quake.
rn.quake.3: Expect aftershocks. When one starts: Drop, Cover, and Hold On.
rn.quake.4: Smell gas or hear hissing? Get everyone outside first. Shut the gas off only if you know how. Once it is off, the utility must turn it back on.
rn.quake.5: No candles, no matches, no lighters. Use a flashlight. Do not flip light switches if you suspect a gas leak.
rn.quake.6: If your building is damaged, get out and stay out. Do not go back inside for belongings.
rn.quake.7: Text instead of calling. Texts get through when networks are jammed. Contact your out-of-area person.
rn.quake.8: Turn on a battery or hand-crank radio for official instructions.
rn.quake.9: Near Puget Sound or the coast? If shaking was long or violent, move to high ground on foot right away. Do not wait for an official warning.
rn.quake.10: Fill your bathtub and containers while water is still running.
rn.quake.911: Call 911 only for a life-threatening emergency. Lines will be overwhelmed.

quake.intro: King County sits on active faults and near the Cascadia Subduction Zone. Plan for two weeks on your own.
quake.s1.h: During shaking: Drop, Cover, Hold On
quake.s1.b: Drop to your hands and knees before the shaking drops you. Cover your head and neck, and get under a sturdy table if one is close. Hold on to it and move with it. If there is no table, get next to an interior wall away from windows and cover your head. Do not run outside. Do not stand in a doorway. In bed, stay there and cover your head with a pillow. In a wheelchair, lock the wheels and cover your head and neck.
quake.s2.b: Shoes first, then check people. Expect aftershocks and drop again when one starts. If you smell gas, get out. Text rather than call. If you are near Puget Sound and the shaking was long or violent, walk to high ground immediately without waiting for a warning.
quake.s3.b: Strap your water heater and bolt tall furniture to studs. Keep shoes and a flashlight under every bed. Pick two meeting places and one out-of-area contact everyone memorizes. Learn where your gas and water shutoffs are, and keep a wrench with the gas meter. Practice Drop, Cover, Hold On with everyone in your home, including kids.
quake.s4.b: A large regional earthquake can damage the roads and bridges that supplies travel on. Emergency services will go to the most severe cases first. Households that can look after themselves for two weeks free up responders for people who cannot.
smoke.intro: Smoke season in King County generally runs through late summer and early fall. The particles in smoke are small enough to reach deep into your lungs.
smoke.s1.b: You do not need to clean your whole home. Pick the room with the fewest windows and doors, close it off, and run an air cleaner there. This is where you sleep and spend the day when the air is bad. A box fan taped to a MERV-13 furnace filter works and costs far less than a purifier. Build it before smoke season starts.
smoke.s2.b: Close windows and doors. Set central heat or AC to recirculate. Close the fresh-air vent on a window unit. Use a damp towel along a drafty door. Do not run a whole-house or attic fan, and do not use a swamp cooler, since both pull outside air in.
smoke.s3.b: Vacuuming, candles, incense, frying, broiling, gas stoves, and smoking all add particles to air you are trying to clean. Skip them while smoke lasts. Use a microwave or an electric kettle instead of the stovetop.
smoke.s4.b: An N95 or KN95 that seals against your face filters smoke particles. Cloth masks, surgical masks, and bandanas do not. Facial hair breaks the seal. Masks do not fit small children, so keep them indoors instead.
smoke.s5.h: Who needs to be more careful
smoke.s5.b: People with asthma, COPD, or heart disease, people who are pregnant, young children, and older adults feel effects sooner and more severely. If that is you or someone in your home, act at lower smoke levels rather than waiting to feel bad. Keep rescue medication where you can reach it.
smoke.s6.b: Trouble breathing, chest pain, a fast heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion means get medical help right away. Call 911 for anything life-threatening.
footer.org: North Creek High School HOSA, in partnership with the Public Health Reserve Corps of Seattle & King County, MRC Unit 503.
footer.privacy_b: We record how the tools are used so we can improve them and report our impact. We store your calculator answers, the zip codes searched, and which actions people commit to. We never collect your name, email, address, phone number, precise location, or IP address. There are no accounts and no advertising trackers. A random number is stored in your browser so we can tell repeat visits apart, and it contains nothing about you. You can clear it any time by clearing your browser data.
footer.disclaimer: This site is a student project. It is educational and is not a substitute for official emergency instructions. In an emergency, follow directions from emergency responders and public health officials.
item.water_supply.name: Drinking water
item.water_supply.note: One gallon per person per day for two weeks. Store it now — you cannot fill containers after a quake breaks the water main.
item.water_storage.name: Water containers
item.water_storage.note: Food-grade containers or sealed store-bought jugs. Write the date on them and replace yearly.
item.water_treat.name: Water treatment supplies
item.water_treat.note: Unscented household bleach or purification tablets. Follow the label instructions exactly.
item.pet_water.name: Extra water for pets
item.pet_water.note: Planning estimate only. Actual need depends on the animal's size — ask your vet.
item.food_supply.name: Shelf-stable food
item.food_supply.note: Two weeks of food needing no cooking and no refrigeration. Choose things your household will actually eat.
item.can_opener.name: Manual can opener
item.can_opener.note: A power outage makes the electric one useless.
item.pet_food.name: Pet food and bowls
item.pet_food.note: Two weeks' worth, stored in a sealed container.
item.rx_buffer.name: Extra prescription medication
item.rx_buffer.note: Ask your pharmacist how to build a buffer. Refill timing varies by insurance and some medications cannot be stockpiled.
item.med_list.name: Written medication list
item.med_list.note: Names, doses, and times, on paper. Include your pharmacy and prescriber. Phones die.
item.med_cooler.name: Cooler for refrigerated medication
item.med_cooler.note: If anything needs refrigeration, plan for cold packs and ask your pharmacist how long it stays usable.
item.first_aid.name: First aid kit
item.first_aid.note: Stock it for what you would actually get: cuts, scrapes, burns, sprains.
item.otc_meds.name: Over-the-counter basics
item.otc_meds.note: Pain reliever, antihistamine, anti-diarrheal, and anything your household uses regularly.
item.n95.name: N95 or KN95 respirators
item.n95.note: Fit matters more than quantity. Cloth and surgical masks do not filter smoke particles.
item.box_fan_filter.name: Box fan and MERV-13 filter
item.box_fan_filter.note: Taped together, this cleans one room's air cheaply. Build it before smoke season, not during.
item.clean_room.name: Choose your clean room
item.clean_room.note: The room with the fewest windows and doors. This is where you go on a smoke day.
item.flashlight.name: Flashlight per person
item.flashlight.note: Headlamps are better since they leave your hands free. Never use candles after an earthquake.
item.batteries.name: Spare batteries
item.batteries.note: Match the sizes your flashlights and radio actually take.
item.radio.name: Battery or hand-crank radio
item.radio.note: When cell networks fail, radio still works.
item.power_bank.name: Charged power bank
item.power_bank.note: Charge it now and top it up every few months.
item.doc_copies.name: Copies of key documents
item.doc_copies.note: ID, insurance, prescriptions, medical info. Paper copies in a sealed bag, plus photos on your phone.
item.cash.name: Small bills in cash
item.cash.note: Card readers need power and internet. Small bills, since nobody will have change.
item.contact_card.name: Out-of-area contact card
item.contact_card.note: One card per person listing an out-of-state contact. Local lines jam; long-distance often gets through.
item.blanket.name: Blanket or sleeping bag
item.blanket.note: One per person. Heat may be out for days.
item.clothes.name: Change of clothes and sturdy shoes
item.clothes.note: Keep shoes and a flashlight under every bed. Broken glass is the most common earthquake injury.
item.hygiene.name: Hygiene supplies
item.hygiene.note: Soap, hand sanitizer, toothbrushes, menstrual supplies, diapers if you need them.
item.sanitation.name: Toilet supplies
item.sanitation.note: Heavy-duty bags, a bucket, and gloves. Sewer lines break in earthquakes and toilets stop working.
item.comfort_items.name: Comfort items
item.comfort_items.note: Games, a book, a favorite toy. Two weeks is a long time, especially for kids.
item.apt_exits.name: Learn two ways out
item.apt_exits.note: Walk both stairwells to the street. Never use the elevator in an earthquake or fire.
item.apt_shutoff.name: Know who shuts off the gas
item.apt_shutoff.note: In most buildings that is management, not you. Get the after-hours number and keep it on paper.
item.apt_gobag.name: Go-bag by the door
item.apt_gobag.note: You may have seconds to leave. Keep one bag where you can grab it on the way out.
item.apt_meetup.name: Two meeting spots
item.apt_meetup.note: One outside your building, one outside the neighborhood in case the block is closed.
item.apt_storage.name: Water you can actually store
item.apt_storage.note: Small stackable containers fit under beds and in closets where a barrel will not.
item.apt_neighbors.name: Know one neighbor
item.apt_neighbors.note: Agree to check on each other. Your neighbors arrive long before any responder does.
item.house_gas.name: Find your gas shutoff
item.house_gas.note: Locate the meter and keep a wrench beside it. Shut it off only if you smell or hear gas — the utility must restore it.
item.house_water.name: Find your water shutoff
item.house_water.note: Know the main valve. Shutting it off protects the clean water still in your heater.
item.house_heater.name: Strap the water heater
item.house_heater.note: It holds many gallons of drinkable water, and it walks off its base in a quake if it is not strapped.
item.house_secure.name: Secure heavy furniture
item.house_secure.note: Strap bookcases, dressers, and the TV to studs. Move heavy objects off shelves above beds.
item.house_storage.name: Use outdoor storage
item.house_storage.note: A sealed bin in the garage or shed keeps supplies reachable if the house is unsafe to enter.
item.house_meetup.name: Two meeting spots
item.house_meetup.note: One outside the house, one outside the neighborhood.
item.pet_carrier.name: Carrier for each animal
item.pet_carrier.note: Label it with your name and phone. A frightened animal will not walk on a leash.
item.pet_records.name: Vaccination records and a photo
item.pet_records.note: Shelters may require proof of vaccination, and a photo of you with your pet proves it is yours.
item.pet_leash.name: Leash, harness, and litter
item.pet_leash.note: Even indoor cats need a carrier and litter.
item.pet_plan.name: Know where pets can go
item.pet_plan.note: Not every shelter takes animals. Check which clean air locations allow pets before you need one.

priv.intro: This site is run by North Creek High School HOSA in partnership with the Public Health Reserve Corps of Seattle & King County, MRC Unit 503. We built it to be useful without knowing who you are. You can use every tool on this site without an account, and most people should.
priv.s1.b: When you use the tools, we record what happened but not who did it: which pages you opened, how long you stayed and how far you scrolled, which reference sections you expanded, the answers you gave the kit calculator, the zip codes searched in the clean air finder, which actions you said you would take this week, and which outside links you followed.
priv.s2.b: We do not collect your name, your address, your phone number, your precise location, or your IP address. We do not use advertising trackers, and we do not sell or share anything with advertisers. The database has no column for any of these, so a future change to this site cannot quietly start storing them.
priv.s3.h: What is stored in your browser
priv.s3.b: Two things are kept in your own browser and never leave it except as described above. A random identifier, which looks like a7f3d9k2b1 and contains nothing about you, lets us tell a returning visitor from a new one. And your checklist progress, so the items you have already ticked off are still ticked when you come back. You can erase both at any time by clearing your browser data for this site. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.
priv.s4.h: If you choose to sign in
priv.s4.b: Signing in is optional and the site works fully without it. Its only purpose is to carry your checklist progress between your own devices. If you sign in with Google, we receive your email address and a user ID from Google, and we store your checklist progress against that ID. We do not receive your Google password. We do not email you, and we will not use your address for anything other than identifying your saved progress.
priv.s5.b: You must be 13 or older to sign in. This is because United States law (COPPA) places strict requirements on collecting personal information from children under 13, and an email address is personal information. Anyone of any age can use every tool on this site anonymously, which collects no personal information at all.
priv.s6.b: To delete a signed-in account and everything stored against it, email us and we will remove it. To remove what is stored in your browser, clear your site data. Anonymous usage records cannot be deleted individually because they are not linked to any person, which is the point of collecting them that way.
priv.s7.b: The site is hosted by Vercel. The database is Supabase. Anonymous usage is mirrored to a Google Sheet that our team can read. Visitor counts come from GoatCounter, which sets no cookies. Map tiles come from OpenStreetMap, which is only contacted if you tap to open the map. Google is involved only if you choose to sign in. Each of these companies sees the traffic needed to do its job and nothing more.
priv.s8.h: Why we collect anything at all
priv.s8.b: Two reasons. It tells us which parts of the site actually help people, so we can improve them. And this is a HOSA competitive project, so we report totals such as how many households built a preparedness plan. Everything reported is a count or an average. No individual is ever identified.
priv.s9.b: Email northcreek.mrc@gmail.com. This is a student project and we will answer.
priv.disclaimer: This site is educational and is not a substitute for official emergency instructions. In an emergency, follow directions from emergency responders and public health officials.
save.auto: Saved on this device. Come back any time and your checklist will be waiting.
auth.h: Use this on your other devices
auth.b: Optional. Sign in and your ticked-off items follow you between your phone, tablet and computer. Everything here works without it.
auth.age_b: You need to be 13 or older to sign in, because signing in shares your email address with us. Everything on this site works without an account at any age.
auth.age_denied: No problem. Every tool here works without an account, and your checklist is still saved on this device.
auth.synced: Your progress now follows you across devices.
auth.error: Sign-in did not work. You can try again, or keep using the site without an account.
auth.privacy_note: We receive only your email address, and use it only to find your saved progress. Read the privacy policy.
auth.merge: We kept the items you had already ticked on this device.
aqi.unavailable: Live air quality is unavailable right now. Check the state air quality map.
aqi.stale: This reading may be out of date.
aqi.do.moderate: Fine for most people. If smoke bothers you, take it easy outdoors.
aqi.do.usg: If you have asthma, heart or lung disease, are pregnant, young or older: shorten time outside and keep medication close.
aqi.do.unhealthy: Everyone should cut back outdoor time. Close windows, set heat or AC to recirculate, and run your clean air room.
aqi.do.very: Stay indoors with filtered air. Avoid outdoor exercise entirely. Wear an N95 if you must go out.
aqi.do.hazardous: Stay inside. If your home cannot get clean, go to a clean air location.
nf.b: The link may be mistyped or out of date. Everything below works.
